subject: AI data use: no-training opt-out, subprocessors & DPA questions
messages:
From: Elena Rojas <elena@medtech.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: PrivacyOps <privacy@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AI data use and training opt-out

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — we appreciated the performance on our clinical note workload. Before we can proceed to legal review, Procurement and Privacy want clarifications on a few items related to data handling for Redwood's hosted offering: 

- No-training/no-improvement commitment: we need an enforceable commitment that customer content (prompts + model outputs + any uploaded documents) will not be used to train or improve Redwood models, or for model evaluation, unless we explicitly opt in. Is this available?

- Prompt/response ownership: confirm that MedTech AI retains all IP rights in prompts and generated outputs.

- Subprocessors: please provide the current subprocessor list and indicate which subprocessors have access to raw customer content.

- Data transfers / residency: we host in the EU for most of our PHI-adjacent data. If data is routed to US infrastructure for inference, we need SCCs or an equivalent mechanism.

- DPA & SOC2 evidence: Procurement asked for your standard DPA and SOC2 report or AICPA letter. If you have a DPA redline we can review that would be helpful.

Can you send your DPA, subprocessor list, and a quick note on the no-training option and how it is implemented (technical controls, retention, logs)?

Best,
Elena
Elena Rojas
Head of Privacy & Compliance
MedTech AI

P.S. Procurement will also want to confirm whether opting out of training has any perf/cost implications (e.g., longer retention, dedicated tenancy, etc.).
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rojas <elena@medtech.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AI data use and training opt-out

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached our current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and the live subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_list.csv). High level answers below; Neha from legal is copied to confirm and provide contract language. 

1) No-training/no-improvement option:
- We offer an explicit contractual option (enterprise add-on) that prohibits Redwood from using Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or evaluate models. By default, hosted API telemetry is used in aggregated/anonymous form for product stability; however, the no-training add-on blocks any model-improvement pipelines from consuming customer-provided content.
- Implementation: content flagged as "no-train" is isolated at the request-routing layer and excluded from offline training datasets. KV cache/prefix caching behavior remains subject to performance SLOs — we can discuss cache TTLs if you prefer stricter eviction.
- Cost/ops: enabling no-training for hosted customers may require additional retention policies (separate audit logs) and in some high-throughput cases a dedicated routing pool (small premium). We’ll mark this in the proposal if you proceed.

2) Ownership:
- Customer retains ownership of prompts and generated responses. Standard clause in our DPA/Terms: "Customer Content and Outputs remain Customer property; Redwood holds no rights to customer-provided prompts or generated outputs except to provide the service and as expressly authorized by Customer."

3) Subprocessors / Access:
- See attached CSV for current list. We call out which subprocessors have access to raw content. Most inference execution is on cloud compute providers (we use managed instances and a small set of infra partners). For the no-training option we can further restrict log aggregation and mask telemetry.

4) Data transfers / SCCs:
- We support SCCs for transfers out of the EU and can include SCC terms in the DPA. For customers with strict residency needs we offer Dedicated or Private deployment to keep inference inside EU only.

Next steps: Neha is going to propose redline language that captures (1) a binding no-training clause and (2) notification timing for subprocessor changes. If you have a procurement questionnaire or a DocuSign PowerForm, send it along and we’ll complete it.

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (standard), subprocessor_list.csv

—
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0119
From: Elena Rojas <elena@medtech.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: PrivacyOps <privacy@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AI data use and training opt-out

Jordan — thanks for the quick response and the attachments. Reviewed with procurement this morning; we have a couple of clarifying asks before we bring this to Legal: 

- Can your team confirm the exact telemetry fields that would still be collected when no-training is enabled (latency, token counts, error rates OK; raw prompt text must be excluded).

- We need explicit language that Redwood will not use outputs for improvement (we've seen vendors claim "metadata" is permitted, which is ambiguous).

- Please confirm SOC2 report availability. If you can provide a read-only link (or a signed AICPA letter), procurement will accept that.

I've attached our procurement PowerForm (DocuSign). We prefer the DPA to include SCCs and a clause that gives us 30 days' notice before any new subprocessor is onboarded that would have access to raw content.

Also: one more question — if we opt into no-training for your hosted API, does that preclude Redwood from running internal model quality monitoring (automated checks that sample outputs for degradation detection)? If so, is there an alternative monitoring-only path that masks prompts/PHI before analysis?

If it's easier, can you have legal send a redline with the suggested no-training text?

Thanks —
Elena
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rojas <elena@medtech.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AI data use and training opt-out — Proposed contract language

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the thoughtful questions. I’ve reviewed Jordan’s notes and drafted precise contract language to address your requirements. Key points below and attached redline (DPA_redlines_jb_neha.docx):

1) No-training / model-improvement prohibition (sample clause):
"Customer Content. Redwood agrees that it will not use, access, or incorporate Customer Content, including prompts, documents, or generated outputs, into any model training, fine-tuning, or evaluation pipeline for the purpose of improving Redwood’s models or services, unless Customer has provided prior written consent. This prohibition applies to both automated and manual processes and applies to Redwood’s subprocessors that have access to Customer Content."

2) Telemetry / monitoring:
- We will enumerate specific telemetry fields in an addendum (latency, token counts, error codes). Raw prompt/response text will be excluded from telemetry when the no-training option is active. For safety/monitoring, we propose an alternate path: Redwood may perform aggregated, pseudonymized checks for system health that do not contain customer-identifiable content. We are happy to build masking rules for PHI if you provide example prompt types.

3) Subprocessors / notice: 
- We will include SCCs for EU transfers and a 30-day notice requirement prior to onboarding any subprocessor that will have access to raw Customer Content. We will also provide an updated subprocessor list on a monthly cadence or upon material change.

4) SOC2:
- We can provide our SOC2 Type II report under NDA via a secure read-only portal. I’ll share the link after we confirm an NDA; alternatively, we can provide an AICPA letter if preferred.

Next steps: I can return a DPA redline (attached) capturing the above. If the DPA redline is acceptable, we can circulate for signatures (DocuSign link below). Please also share any example prompts or categories you want us to treat as high-sensitivity so we can confirm masking rules.

DocuSign (MedTech PowerForm): https://na123.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na123&id=3a8f9b

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
